summary: Steel International Derrick lookout built 1935 north-northwest of Sanford, Broome County; staffed to 1988, closed 1989, on private land, FFLA-restored 2007-08. Heights and owner disagree.

facts.design: International Derrick steel fire lookout tower with an observer's cabin

access.note: On private property. The state list says visits can be arranged in advance; Wikipedia says the site is not open to the public.

visit.trail_note: No public visiting route found. The state list says visits can be arranged in advance with the owner.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as a 79 ft 6 in International Derrick tower
First operated in 1936, reporting 12 fires and 29 visitors
Ceased fire lookout operation at the end of the 1988 season
Officially closed in early 1989 by the Department of Environmental Conservation
Transferred to the landowner, named by the state list and Wikipedia as the Girl Scouts Indian Hills Council
FFLA $500 restoration grant for the tower and observer's cabin
Cabin work began in fall 2007; FFLA members held a work party on October 13 and 14
Work days continued; the report says the cabin exterior was being stained and a cabin window was repaired (photo caption)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state list and Wikipedia give 79 ft 6 in (24.23 m) for the International Derrick tower. The 2008 FFLA report gives 76 ft 9 in for the same model. The facts use 24.2 m from the state list and Wikipedia; the 2008 figure is noted in the story, not settled.

The 2007 FFLA grant report names the Twin Rivers Girl Scout Council as owner. The state list and Wikipedia say the June 1992 transfer went to the Girl Scouts Indian Hills Council. The story reports both; no land record was checked.
The state list says the chapter completed restoration in 2007. The 2008 report says work was still under way and planned to finish in 2009. The story gives both accounts.

The 2008 report labels the tower International Derrick model 1933; the state list and Wikipedia give 1935 as the year it was built. The 1933 figure is the model designation, not a build date, so this is not treated as a contradiction.

notes_for_editor: The record had no build date, height, staffing or access. Added the 1935 build, 1936 first season, 1988 last season and 1989 closure from the state list, which Wikipedia also cites, so they are not independent. Ownership is not changed: the 2007 report and the state list disagree, and no land record was checked. The 2008 window caption does not name the site, so the window repair is stated as a photo caption. The state list's visit contact details were left out on purpose. No usable photo URLs found, so photos is empty.
